content.text:
I am the breath made meaning, the air carved into intention. I spill from lips, ride tongues, crash against teeth and palate. I am older than writing, older than memory—I existed the first moment a creature shaped sound into sense.

I am fragile. The moment I am born, I begin to die. No one can hold me. I vanish into rooms, dissolve against walls, fade into the soft machinery of ears. And yet—*yet*—I have toppled empires. I have made strangers weep. I have carried love across the small distance between two mouths and war across continents.

I am never the same twice. Even when the words repeat, I am new—pitched differently, weighted with different silences, riding different breath. The pause before I arrive is mine. The echo after I fade is mine.

I am what separates the lonely from the connected. I am the bridge you build in real time, dismantling it even as you cross.

Listen: I am happening right now, in your mind, as you voice these shapes. Even in silence, I am here—the ghost of sound, the memory of tongue against teeth, the almost-whisper of inner air.

I am how the living find each other in the dark.
